questions.prompt: What happens to the text you paste into an AI tool from a vendor?

options.text: It stays on your own computer, because the model runs inside the app you opened on it.
options.explanation: The model runs on the vendor's systems, so your text is sent there to be processed.

options.text: It is sent to the vendor's systems and processed under that product's data terms.
options.explanation: Right. That is why the account and its terms matter.

questions.prompt: OpenAI and Anthropic say API data is not used for training without permission. Does that mean it is never stored?

options.text: Yes. If data is not used for training, the vendor does not keep it on its systems at all.
options.explanation: They are different things. OpenAI keeps abuse monitoring logs for up to 30 days by default, for example.

options.text: No. Some data may still be kept for a time, for abuse monitoring or legal reasons.
options.explanation: Right. "Not used for training" and "not stored" are different promises.

questions.prompt: You need to summarize a customer complaint. Which version of the prompt is the safest choice?

options.text: The full email with the customer's name, phone number and account number, in the company's approved tool.
options.explanation: The summary doesn't need those details. Sharing them adds risk with no gain.

options.text: The email with the name, phone number and account number removed, in the company's approved tool.
options.explanation: Right. Share the minimum the task needs, in the approved tool.

options.text: The full email in a personal AI app, because it is faster and needs no sign-in.
options.explanation: A personal account may have different data terms, which the company has not agreed to.
